correctness.rationale: For the uniquely coupled stationary two-orientation PDMP, addition and subtraction of the forward equations give J'= -r p+r delta_0 and H'=-(r+2lambda)d. Reflection and zero endpoint flux force J(0+)=r/2, hence d(0+)=r/(2Sigma) and the exact signed cusp slope. On the positive half, U=fp_+, W=bp_- satisfy a first-order current system and 0<W<U. An integrating factor gives a finite positive endpoint coefficient; a backward integral for W gives W/U -> lambda/(r+lambda). Thus p ~ C delta^((r+lambda)/g'(v*)-1). The independent cusp/edge strict inequalities produce the iff Sigma<1/sqrt(2) shear-thinning coexistence threshold. The r=0 curvature follows by differentiating the zero-current equation. Seven ODE cases pass 21 numerical comparisons; these do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The source study observes a transition from center dips to cusps and from divergent to vanishing endpoint densities. The exact one-sided slope makes both the transition rate and cusp amplitude calculable without solving the stationary density, and its combination with the independent endpoint exponent identifies a natural observable coexistence regime. The iff activity threshold Sigma<1/sqrt(2) for shear thinning is a structural boundary, not an arbitrary numerical parameter slice. The zero-reset morphology reversal for 1/2<lambda<1 demonstrates a genuinely singular local effect of even rare velocity-reset events. All implications are confined to local stationary-shape observables and do not imply global mode counts.
